# Observability

> Optional Sentry error and log reporting, wired identically into the admin service and the agent runtime through the shared `lib/sentry.ts` helper.

## Overview

The admin service (`service: "admin"`) and the agent runtime (`service: "agent"`) can each report to Sentry when `SENTRY_DSN` is set in their own environment. Each process reads its own `SENTRY_DSN`; there is no shared or global toggle. When `SENTRY_DSN` is unset (the default), or when `NODE_ENV` is `"test"`, Sentry is fully inert: no init call, zero telemetry, zero overhead. The test guard keeps error-path test assertions from reaching a real Sentry project. `scripts/test-env-preload.ts`, loaded through the `[test]` preload in `bunfig.toml`, forces `NODE_ENV=test`, and the `test` scripts in `package.json` and `admin/package.json` also carry a `NODE_ENV=test` prefix.

Both services share the same init options and scrub hooks through `buildSentryInitOptions()` and `initSentry()` in `lib/sentry.ts` (see [shared-lib.md](shared-lib.md)), so behavior is identical regardless of which one reports:

- The agent runtime calls `initSentry({ service: "agent", agentId })` in `runtime/boot.ts`, right after its console prefixing is installed, so Sentry wraps the already-prefixed console.
- The admin service calls `initSentry({ service: "admin" })` at the start of `startAdmin()` and mounts `@sentry/hono`'s `sentry()` middleware on the root app, built from the same `buildSentryInitOptions()` result, only when `SENTRY_DSN` is set.

The environment tag is `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT`, falling back to `NODE_ENV`, then `"production"`.

## What is collected

When `SENTRY_DSN` is set, a service reports to Sentry. The table summarizes what is captured and what is redacted.

| Data | Captured by Sentry? |
|---|---|
| Unhandled exceptions and 5xx errors, with stack traces | Yes |
| `console.log` / `console.warn` / `console.error` calls, forwarded as structured logs | Yes |
| Request path and method for HTTP errors | Yes |
| Caller identity (which admin key, agent token or session triggered an admin API error) | Yes, in the logged error line |
| Tags: `service` (always) and `agent_id` (agent runtime) | Yes |
| `Authorization` and `Cookie` header values | Redacted, replaced with `[Filtered]` regardless of configuration |
| Request or response bodies | No, never attached to an event |
| The live value of any secret-shaped env var | Redacted, scrubbed wherever it appears, including nested inside longer strings |

Secret redaction compares against the live process values of the names in `SECRET_ENV_VARS` (`lib/secret-env-vars.ts`, the same list the admin service uses to mark env keys as `secret`). It is an exact string match on this process's own secrets, applied to events (`scrubEvent`) and structured logs (`scrubLog`).

**Tags** are set once at init through the static `initialScope` in `buildSentryInitOptions()`. `ErrorCapturingClient.withScope` (also in `lib/sentry.ts`) lets a caller fork a Sentry scope so extra tags stay local to one operation instead of mutating global state; the admin pool-timeout capture below uses it.

### Claude session error classification

Every runtime call site that reports a `claude` CLI runner error (`runtime/cron-failure-reporter.ts`, `runtime/health.ts` and `runtime/slack.ts`) goes through `reportClaudeError(sentryClient, err)` in `runtime/claude.ts` instead of calling `captureException` directly. It classifies the error first:

- A `ClaudeTimeoutError` with `reason: "ceiling"` is the intentional one-hour hard-ceiling backstop firing on a legitimately long-running session, not a defect. It is downgraded to `sentryClient.captureMessage()`, so it stays visible in Sentry without creating an actionable Issue that would keep reappearing as regressed.
- Every other error, including a `ClaudeTimeoutError` with `reason: "idle"` (a genuine hang), is reported unchanged through `captureException(err)`.

Any new call site that can receive a thrown `ClaudeTimeoutError` should report through `reportClaudeError` to keep this classification consistent. See [agent-runtime.md](agent-runtime.md#running-claude-claudets) for the timeouts.

The runtime also strips `SENTRY_DSN` from the environment it passes to each spawned `claude` process (`runtime/claude.ts`), so a Claude Code session, and anything it runs, cannot construct its own Sentry client from the agent's ambient environment. This does not affect the agent's own reporting.

### Admin pool starvation diagnostics

The admin service instruments its `pg.Pool` using [`lib/pool-observability.ts`](../lib/pool-observability.ts), wired in `admin/src/prisma-client.ts`. This is observability only: pool size and queries are unchanged.

- **Route context.** A middleware (`routeContextMiddleware()`) records the HTTP method and matched route pattern for each request, so pool events can be attributed to a route.
- **Hold tracking.** `pool.connect()` is wrapped so a connection held longer than `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_POOL_HOLD_THRESHOLD_MS` (default 2000) logs `pg connection held past threshold` with the route, `heldMs` and pool stats.
- **Monitor.** Every `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_POOL_MONITOR_INTERVAL_MS` (default 30000) the pool is checked and `pg pool has waiting clients` is logged while any client is queued. The monitor is stopped, and `pool.connect` restored, during graceful shutdown.
- **Sentry.** When an unhandled error captured by the admin API is a pool timeout (Prisma `P2028`, "Unable to start a transaction", or a pg connection timeout), the event carries a `pg_pool` context (`total`, `idle`, `waiting`, `max`, `route`) and `route` and `server_name` tags. Other errors are captured unchanged.

Invalid or non-positive threshold values are ignored and the defaults apply. See [admin-service.md](admin-service.md) for how the admin process boots and shuts down.

## Disabling Sentry

Unset `SENTRY_DSN` (or never set it) for the service in question. This is the default; no other configuration is needed to keep a service fully offline from Sentry. Sentry is also disabled automatically whenever `NODE_ENV` is `"test"`, even if `SENTRY_DSN` is present in the environment.

## Self-hosted Sentry

`SENTRY_DSN` works with a self-hosted Sentry instance the same way it works with Sentry's SaaS offering: point it at your own instance and project's DSN. No other configuration changes are needed.

## Configuration reference

- `SENTRY_DSN` and `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT`: per-service, optional. Admin variables are summarized in [admin-service.md](admin-service.md#configuration); the agent runtime environment reference is [configuration-agent.md](configuration-agent.md).
- `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_POOL_HOLD_THRESHOLD_MS` and `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_POOL_MONITOR_INTERVAL_MS`: admin pool diagnostics, described above.
